name: Historic Lakhori Brick Masonry (Badshahi / Thin Flat Terracotta Brick)
traditional_use: Vaults, arches, linings, and pavilions in Sultanate, Mughal, and regional Nawabi baolis and tanks across northern and eastern India.

moisture_behavior.breathability: High vapor permeability through open ceramic micro-capillaries
moisture_behavior.summary: High porosity and thin cross-section require lime mortar with equal or higher breathability.

mechanical_characteristics.stiffness: Low to moderate modulus of elasticity
mechanical_characteristics.ductility: Brittle, susceptible to crumbling under stress concentration
mechanical_characteristics.sacrificial_behavior: Historic substrate; mortar joints (typically 15-25mm thick) must be softer than the brick
mechanical_characteristics.summary: Because joint thickness often equals brick thickness, the mortar system dominates overall structural behavior.

thermal_characteristics.summary: Surkhi aggregate is made from identical crushed terracotta, ensuring thermal expansion equilibrium.

chemical_considerations.soluble_salts_risk: Vulnerable to salt fretting and surface spalling if dampness cannot evaporate
chemical_considerations.reactivity_with_limestone: Pozzolanic bonding between brick faces and hydraulic lime mortar
chemical_considerations.summary: Chemical bonding with lime mortar creates a monolithic yet ductile structural masonry mass.

heritage_compatibility.iks_alignment: Traditional hand-moulded alluvial clay fired in country clamps with herbal water tempering

limitations: Modern standard bricks (75mm thick) are dimensionally incompatible with historic lakhori brickwork (20-30mm thick).
Application of Portland cement mortar destroys lakhori bricks by causing edge crushing and salt blister spalling.
